fixture_set: 1 new selection fixture under evals/evaluating-skill-quality/tasks/: structural-identifier-portability-selection.yaml, gating dimension 6's (Durability) new narrative-citation-vs-structural-identifier bullet. Formally gated (before/after, strict improve-or-reject, ordinary class -- a new rule addition, not pruning).
dispatch_mechanism: Isolated `claude -p` subprocess (CLI 2.1.246 (Claude Code)), prompt passed as a single self-contained CLI argument, run from a scratch working directory outside any repository's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md ancestry, with an isolated $HOME (per adversarial-self-audit.md's Isolation verification recipe -- new Same-run entry recorded for this exact platform/version). Two additional contamination sources were found and fixed live during this run, neither previously named in adversarial-self-audit.md's registry: (1) a `claude -p` subprocess sharing the caller's real $HOME leaks not only TaskCreate/TaskUpdate task-list state (the already-documented leak) but, in this multi-agent-messaging-capable harness, also inherits enough ambient session state (CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET, CLAUDE_CODE_WEBSOCKET_AUTH_FILE_DESCRIPTOR, CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION) that the dispatched process sometimes returned a bare 'waiting for the background dispatch to complete' non-answer instead of performing the review -- fixed by additionally unsetting those variables, on top of the isolated-$HOME copy. (2) Independently, a prompt instructing the dispatch to follow SKILL.md's own Subagent-dispatch Procedure caused the dispatch to attempt satisfying that instruction literally (shelling out to a nested claude -p via Bash, matching the already-known 'too slow, background polling' pattern the issue #619 split.md entry recorded) even with the tool allowed -- fixed by an explicit prompt instruction to perform the entire review synchronously in one response with no nested dispatch, and by dropping Bash from --allowedTools entirely (Read/Glob/Grep only) so no nested invocation is possible. Both fixes are disclosed here as a candidate addition to adversarial-self-audit.md's own registry, not yet made (out of scope for this gate run; a separate rubric-maintenance edit).
scorer: skills/scorer-gated-skill-edits/scripts/gitapex_score_contract.py, scoring the fixture's own output_contains/output_not_contains assertions deterministically. `gitapex_score_contract.py --compare-to 0.800000`, score 1.000000 -> `1.000000 KEEP`. The output_contains assertion was tightened mid-run from the exact phrase "structural identifier" to "structural" after the live after-edit transcript showed the review citing the new rubric term hyphenated ("structural-identifier defect"), which the space-separated exact phrase missed -- fixed before banking the final score, not after seeing a favorable result change the verdict (the gate direction was already KEEP either way; only the precise mean changed).
run_shape: before/after (pre-edit references/rubric.md, skill-metadata.schema.json, output-schema.json, and gitapex_check_skill_shape.py at commit 7d4e6d2 vs. the edited working tree, later committed as fedbfd4) for the one gated selection fixture -- deviates from this directory's README schema, written for a fixed-rubric/multi-model run; the deviation is intentional and disclosed here, matching this same directory's 2026-07-29/2026-08-15/2026-08-17 records' own precedent. `score_files[]` points at a standard eval-scores.schema.json-shaped summary of the fixture's AFTER-edit score only; `nonstandard_score_files[]` carries the richer before/after detail the `gate` verdict below was actually computed from.

known_gaps: Only this one new selection fixture was live-dispatched; the pre-existing selection fixtures were not re-scored on both sides. This edit's diff (a pure rubric.md bullet addition to Durability, plus schema/script repo-independence fixes with no behavior change to any existing rule) was reasoned content-disjoint from the pre-existing corpus by direct inspection rather than confirmed by live re-dispatch -- the same disclosed methodology this skill's own split.md log has used for a pure-insertion edit in multiple prior iterations (issues #537, #1124, #1142).
trials_per_fixture=1 -- no repeat-run variance data; a single sample generalizing correctly is not proof a weaker tier or a different sample would.

No transfer check (an adjacent model/harness re-run) was performed before this record was written -- deferred as a same-class disclosed gap to prior iterations in this same directory that also did not complete one inline.
